monument.purpose: Hero wordmark, pinned chapter words (Words/Code/Music/Jonathan), closing CTA slab. Type at architectural scale on a bare ground — the only place type behaves as image rather than heading. A BAND not one step: longer strings step down (hero 17vw, chapter 21vw, long-word 13vw, close 12vw) so the line never wraps or collides. One per viewport, nothing competing.

hud-label.purpose: Glass-HUD corner consoles only — the Storm Door link and the scroll-tracked beat readout. Tracked micro-caps from the shared genome chrome. Never reading content.

display.purpose: Inner-page hero H1, section H2s, card/item titles, blockquotes. Balanced with text-wrap: balance.

body.purpose: Reading copy on Daylight sections. 65–75ch measure, 1.75 line-height.

label.purpose: Kickers, nav links, button/meta labels only. Never full sentences.

hand.purpose: Notecard scrap and hand-numerals only — a deliberate handwritten-object moment, never body copy.

shadows.name: photo-lift
shadows.purpose: Taped photographs — physically pinned to the page.

shadows.name: card-hover
shadows.purpose: Work-grid item cards, hover only, paired with translateY(-3px).

shadows.name: button-glow
shadows.purpose: Primary button at rest; deepens to 0 14px 38px rgba(188,90,36,0.45) on hover.

shadows.name: notecard
shadows.purpose: Handwritten scrap, paired with a 1.5deg rotation.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for hover lifts, arrow slides, pill fills.

motion.name: reveal-duration
motion.purpose: Scroll-reveal fade+rise for .reveal sections, via IntersectionObserver at 12% threshold.

motion.name: seal-spin
motion.purpose: The subscribe-section seal badge's slow rotation; paused under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:0.55rem; font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size:0.92rem; letter-spacing:0.02em; text-decoration:none; cursor:pointer; padding:0.95rem 1.6rem; border-radius:999px; border:0; background:#A53B1F; color:#FDF7EE; transition: transform 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1), background 0.4s, box-shadow 0.4s; box-shadow: 0 8px 30px rgba(188,90,36,0.35); } .ds-btn-primary:hover, .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { background:#7E2F16; transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: 0 14px 38px rgba(188,90,36,0.45); } .ds-btn-arrow { transition: transform 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover .ds-btn-arrow { transform: translateX(4px); }

components.name: Taped Photo
components.description: The core physical-object motif — photo on cream paper, torn-kraft backing, tape pinning it down, rotated -1.4deg.
components.css: .ds-taped { position:relative; display:inline-block; padding:0.7rem; background:#E7DEC9; box-shadow: 0 18px 46px rgba(57,53,51,0.22); transform: rotate(-1.4deg); } .ds-taped img { display:block; width:260px; height:auto; } .ds-tape { position:absolute; width:104px; height:30px; background:rgba(224,212,178,0.5); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(57,53,51,0.12); z-index:2; } .ds-tape-tl { top:-13px; left:16%; transform: rotate(-7deg); } .ds-tape-br { bottom:-12px; right:14%; transform: rotate(-6deg); }

narrative.overview: The whole site is built as if it's the porch before the letter arrives — the room you sit in before the Storm Door lands in your inbox Saturday morning. Nothing here is engineered to convert; it's laid out like objects a person actually kept: a taped photograph, a torn scrap of notepaper, a hand-inked underline, a ledger line. The two skins never blend — Daylight (warm eggshell, #EDEAE3) is the reading room, unhurried and paper-toothed; Lamplit (#2C2926 charcoal, filmic photography) is the threshold — hero, interstitials, the subscribe close. Crossing between them is deliberate, like walking from the porch into the house at dusk. This system explicitly rejects: generic AI-slop SaaS marketing (cream/gradient body backgrounds, identical card grids, gradient text, glassmorphism-as-decoration), anything cold or corporate-feeling, and — as standing project doctrine — any crypto/blockchain/decentralization-as-technology visual language, even incidentally.
keyCharacteristics: Two skins in tension (Daylight reading / Lamplit threshold), never merged into one flat tone
Depth read as physical objects (tape, torn paper, grain) rather than digital drop-shadows
Serif-on-serif display/body pairing, one sans-serif reserved for labels only
Every texture handmade-coded: nothing that reads as a flat vector standing in for the real thing

rules.name: The One-Accent Rule
rules.body: Rust is the only color allowed to mean action or attention. Ochre and denim are atmosphere, never competing CTAs.

rules.name: The No-Flat-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth never comes from a generic box-shadow alone — every elevated element is a physical object whose shadow reads as paper lifting off a surface, warm-tinted, never neutral gray or cool black.

rules.name: The Two-Serif Rule
rules.body: Only Bodoni Moda and Libre Baskerville carry reading content. The sans-serif label font never appears above label size and never carries a full sentence.

rules.name: The Object, Not the Layer Rule
rules.body: A shadow only appears where a physical object metaphor justifies it. Flat sections and body text never carry a shadow.

dos: Do keep rust as the only color that means action — buttons, active states, the one CTA per section.
Do justify every shadow with a physical object; nothing gets a shadow just because it's a container.
Do keep Daylight and Lamplit fully separate — no gradient blending one into the other within a single section.
Do use the torn-clip / grain / taped-photo vocabulary for anything that needs to feel kept, not built.
donts: Don't use a cream/gradient body background as a generic warm default — Ground (#EDEAE3) is a named, specific surface.
Don't build identical repeating card grids with icon + heading + text.
Don't use gradient text, glassmorphism-as-decoration, or generic SaaS-marketing scaffolding.
Don't let the sans-serif label font carry a full sentence or appear above 0.92rem.
Don't mix cool denim into more than the one dedicated cool-room section.
